extracted.intended_audience: patent owners and patent practitioners preparing and filing requests for supplemental examination with the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and filing a USPTO request for supplemental examination under 37 CFR 1.610, including required fees, required content (lists, copies, translations, claim identifications), and the detailed explanation of how each submitted item of information applies to each identified claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of required fees at filing
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for supplemental examination must be accompanied by the fee for filing a request for supplemental examination (37 CFR 1.20(k)(1)), the fee for ex parte reexamination ordered as a result of a supplemental examination (37 CFR 1.20(k)(2)), and any applicable document size fees (37 CFR 1.20(k)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all required fees are not paid at filing the request is defective and will not be granted a filing date; fees may be refunded per 37 CFR 1.610(d). Fees qualify for a 60% reduction for small entities and an 80% reduction for micro entities (see MPEP § 509.04). The reexamination fee (1.20(k)(2)) will be refunded if the supplemental examination certificate indicates no substantial new question of patentability (SNQ) and reexamination is not ordered. If notified of missing fees, timely payment of corrected fee may restore the filing date as the receipt date of the corrected request; otherwise the request will not receive a filing date and processing is terminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document size fees applicability and calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Document size fees (37 CFR 1.20(k)(3)) apply only to non-patent documents having more than 20 pages; patent documents (U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications, published international patent applications, foreign patents and patent application publications, and translations of non-English patent documents) are not subject to the document size fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each non-patent document is counted separately even if designated as an exhibit to a declaration. Non-patent documents of 21–50 pages are subject to the 21–50 page fee; documents >50 pages are also subject to an additional fee for each additional 50-page increment or fraction thereof. Blank pages are counted. Fees are not pro-rated and are calculated per document. Examples in the MPEP illustrate counting multiple documents and additional increments; patent owners are encouraged to redact lengthy documents to include only relevant portions unless redaction removes necessary context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of the patent number
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must include an identification of the number of the patent for which supplemental examination is requested (37 CFR 1.610(b)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the patent number clearly so the Office can identify the patent to be examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of items of information submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must include a list of the items of information that are requested to be considered, reconsidered, or corrected (37 CFR 1.610(b)(2)). Where appropriate the list must meet the requirements of 37 CFR 1.98(b) (e.g., include publication date; for U.S. patents identify inventor, patent number, and issue date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list must include each item submitted with or as part of the request (including internal discussions in the request body by page number and brief description). The list must be limited to items for which a separate, detailed explanation is provided under 1.610(b)(5) and for which copies are provided when required under 1.610(b)(7). If items are listed without the required explanation or copy, the request may be denied a filing date and a notice of noncompliant request may be mailed. Patent owners are strongly encouraged to use Part B of Office Form PTO/SB/59 to provide the list.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of prior or concurrent post-patent Office proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must include a list identifying any other prior or concurrent post-patent Office proceedings involving the patent, including the type of proceeding, the identifying number (e.g., control number or reissue application number), and filing date (37 CFR 1.610(b)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Types of proceedings may include ex parte/inter partes reexamination, reissue, interference, supplemental examination, post-grant review, inter partes review, covered business method review, etc. Patent owners should use PTO/SB/59. If a post-patent proceeding is discovered after filing, 37 CFR 1.620(d) requires prompt notification to the Office; see MPEP § 2820.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of each claim to be examined
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must identify each claim of the patent for which supplemental examination is requested (37 CFR 1.610(b)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because patentability issues pertain to claims, the patent owner must identify the specific claims to be examined so the Office can determine whether any item of information raises a SNQ affecting those claims. Patent owners are encouraged to specify which items of information apply to which claims; if not specified, the Office will assume all identified claims are to be considered in light of every listed item of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate, detailed explanation of relevance and manner of applying each item to each claim
rubrics_metrics.description: For each item listed under 1.610(b)(2) the request must include a separate, detailed explanation of the relevance and manner of applying that item to each claim for which supplemental examination is requested (37 CFR 1.610(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The explanation must explain for each claim either (1) what the item teaches with respect to that claim, or (2) which teachings in the item an examiner may consider important in determining patentability. Citations to particular portions or figures should be included. Ideally provide a claim chart comparing each claim limitation with the teachings of each item. General statements not tied to claim limitations are insufficient. Provide separate explanations for dependent claims or expressly incorporate the independent claim explanation for dependent claims. Use headings and subheadings (identify each item and which claims are discussed); examples of acceptable headings are provided. Do not combine the required detailed explanation with optional patentability arguments (e.g., 1.610(c) discussions) because doing so can obscure the required explanation and risk a finding of noncompliance and loss of the filing date. Be comprehensive to frame potential issues and assist examiner review. The Office may accept imperfect explanations if the meaning is readily understood, but failure to provide required explanations will lead to a Notice of Noncompliant Supplemental Examination Request (37 CFR 1.610(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies and translations of items of information
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must include a copy of each item of information listed in 1.610(b)(2), accompanied by a written English translation of all necessary and pertinent parts of any non-English item of information (37 CFR 1.610(b)(7)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies must be legible and comply with 37 CFR 1.52 and 1.615. Items that form part of the discussion within the body of the request per 1.605(b) are not required to be separately submitted. Copies of U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications are not required but may be submitted. See MPEP § 609.04(a) for translation guidance. Providing copies and translations helps the examiner consider materials within the three-month statutory period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary for documents over 50 pages
rubrics_metrics.description: A request must include a summary of the relevant portions of any submitted document (other than the request) that is over 50 pages in length (37 CFR 1.610(b)(8)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary must include citations to the particular pages containing the relevant portions. This assists the Office in treating lengthy documents within the three-month supplemental examination time period. Patent owners are encouraged to redact lengthy documents to relevant portions unless redaction would remove necessary context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of owner(s) and proof of entire ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must identify the owner(s) of the entire right, title, and interest in the patent and include a submission by the patent owner in compliance with 37 CFR 3.73(c) establishing entirety of ownership (37 CFR 1.610(b)(9)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplemental examination request must be filed by the owner(s) of the entire interest because a patent's scope may change during any resulting reexamination. All parties with ownership interest are treated as a composite 'patent owner' and must act together. In rare circumstances, the Office may permit less than all owners to file if a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.183 waiving provisions of 3.71 and 3.73(c) is filed (see MPEP § 2803). An ADS under 37 CFR 1.76 cannot be submitted in supplemental examination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Office Form PTO/SB/59 encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/59 is recommended to assist persons filing requests for supplemental examination as a transmittal form, list of items of information, list of prior or concurrent post-patent Office proceedings, and cover sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of the form helps ensure the request contains the information the Office expects and may reduce clerical defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on satisfying detailed explanation by incorporation or third-party papers
rubrics_metrics.description: The detailed explanation requirement under 37 CFR 1.610(b)(5) cannot be satisfied by incorporating by reference a paper from another proceeding or by relying on a paper by a third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplemental examination request must stand on its own. Incorporation by reference would require the Office to review other proceedings to determine compliance, which would impede the Office's ability to complete supplemental examination within the three-month statutory period. For example, an Office action from another proceeding cannot be used as the detailed explanation for the current request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy and formatting requirements for the patent copy
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must include a copy of the patent (and any disclaimer or certificate) reproduced so specification and claims are in double-column format and drawing pages and front page are presented as in the printed patent; copies must be single-sided (each page plainly written on only one side).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include any certificate of correction, extension, supplemental examination certificate, post-grant review certificate, ex parte/inter partes reexamination certificates, disclaimers, etc., because they generally become part of the patent. Use a full copy of the printed patent if desired; do not submit two-sided copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office notification and cure of noncompliance; potential loss of filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request fails to comply with filing date requirements (e.g., missing explanations, missing fees, missing copies), the Office may mail a Notice of Noncompliant Supplemental Examination Request under 37 CFR 1.610(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner timely files a corrected request that addresses all defects identified in the notice and otherwise complies with 1.605, 1.615, and the section, the filing date will be the receipt date of the corrected request. If fees or required materials are not timely received after notification, the request will not receive a filing date, processing will be terminated, and refunds made as appropriate.
